<h3><a href="news/cna-applied-in-environmental-psychology.html">CNA applied in Environmental Psychology</a></h3>
<p>Henrik Johansson Rehn, Alexandre Sukhov, Lars E. Olsson, and Margareta Friman use CNA to explore the "window of opportunity" for car use reduction and to identify the causal pathways that lead people to reduce their car use.</p>
</div>

<div class="cna-news-meta"><span class="cna-news-dateline">03.08.2026</span></div>
<h3><a href="news/cna-applied-in-firearm-policy.html">How local prevention efforts and state regulations reduce fatal shootings</a></h3>
<p>Daniel C. Semenza, Edward J. Miech, Brielle Savage, and Devon Ziminski use CNA to examine how combinations of city-level prevention efforts and state-level firearm policies link to fatal shooting rates across 100 US cities.</p>
</div>
</article>

<h3><a href="news/factor-selection-guidance-for-configurational-comparative-methods.html">Guidance for factor selection in configurational comparative analysis</a></h3>
<p>Laura Caci, Kathrin Blum, Lauren Clack, and Bianca Albers provide guidance on selecting factors for Coincidence Analysis and other configurational comparative methods, offering a four-stage approach for implementation researchers.</p>
</div>
</article>

<h3><a href="news/cna-applied-in-chicago-life-expectancy.html">CNA applied to low life expectancy in Chicago</a></h3>
<p>John Rich, Edward Miech, and colleagues apply CNA to identify the social factors that link to low life expectancy across Chicago's 77 community areas, finding that low birth weight, unemployment, and non-fatal shootings combine across alternative pathways to the outcome.</p>
</div>
</article>
